# Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338) — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338). Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-02 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] ITMS-90338 'Non-public API usage' is an automated check that matches symbols referenced by any Mach-O in the bundle (including third-party frameworks and static libs) against Apple's private-symbol list. Apple's remedy text: rename source methods that collide with listed private APIs, or remove static libraries containing them; the cause is often a bundled third-party framework that needs updating. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/733322 · keywords: Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338) · also: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/20026

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Removing an unneeded extension module from the bundle (e.g. _tkinter .so) cleared a non-public-API rejection for a Mac app embedding Python; Apple's reply stated non-public or deprecated APIs are not permitted and offered appeal to the App Review Board. (low confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/758567

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Guideline 2.5.1 says apps may only use public APIs and must run on the currently shipping OS; 2.5.2 says apps must be self-contained in their bundles, may not read/write outside the container, and may not download, install, or execute code that introduces or changes features. Educational code-teaching apps get a narrow exception. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338) · also: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/120522
- [statement] Embedded Python has been rejected for symbols the author never called: Python 3.9 libformw/libpanelw (ncurses) and posix_spawn symbols cited under Guideline 2.5.1 (March 2021, later validated without comment after the developer raised it), and Tcl.framework symbols via _tkinter.cpython-39-darwin.so (July 2024). (medium confidence) — https://bugs.python.org/issue43374 · keywords: Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338) · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/758567
- [statement] Python 3.12 added the literal string 'itms-services' to Lib/urllib/parse.py (and its .pyc); Apple's scan flagged it under Guideline 2.5.2 ('installed or launched executable code'). CPython added a --with-app-store-compliance configure option (issue opened 2024-06-14) to patch it out; removing the string from a bundled copy let an update pass. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-06-14) — https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/120522 · keywords: Guideline 2.5 public APIs and bundled interpreter and private-API string scan (ITMS-90338) · also: https://medium.com/top-python-libraries/python-program-banned-from-apple-app-store-due-to-a-single-string-a67df6d8fa66
- [statement] Tkinter remains unshippable on the Mac App Store in CPython 3.9-3.14: libtk8.6.dylib references _NSWindowDidOrderOnScreenNotification; no fix as of the issue opened 2025-01-23. A menu-bar utility without Tk should exclude tkinter/Tcl/Tk from the py2app bundle. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-23) — https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/129247
- [statement] Embedding Python and shipping to the Mac App Store has worked in practice: an embedded, signed interpreter keeps the sandbox and hardened runtime; old py2app versions produced invalid Python.framework bundles, and py2app 0.26 replaced a private symbol in its stub executable with a public API. (low confidence) — https://github.com/davidfstr/Python-in-Mac-App-Store
